text: More than 3,000 years ago, many peoples lived in the lands where Bulgaria and Romania are today.
The Greeks called them Thracians, and the poet Homer was the first to write down their name.
src: Thracian culture emerged in the early Bronze Age and flourished in the 3rd and 2nd millennia BCE / Bulgaria, Romania, North Macedonia, northern Greece and European Turkey
“Thracians” is the name the ancient Greeks gave to many peoples of the eastern Balkans / The first record of the name is in Homer’s Iliad

text: They lived in about 200 groups, mostly in simple villages, and were rarely united.
One king, Seuthes III, built their only city, Seuthopolis.
src: some 200 tribes of south-eastern Europe who shared much of their culture but were rarely united in one state / Most Thracians lived in simple, open villages
their only polis was Seuthopolis, the capital founded by Seuthes III around 330 BCE

text: The Thracians are thought to be the first to worship the god of wine, whom the Greeks called Dionysus.
Many men and women had tattoos, and the Thracians were known for their poetry and music.
src: The Thracians are considered the first to worship the god of wine, called Dionysus in Greek and Zagreus in Thracian
Tattooing was common among both men and women / Greek and Roman writers ... still noted the sophistication of their poetry and music

text: About 2,500 years ago, more than 40 Thracian groups joined together in the Odrysian Kingdom.
They were skilled horse riders, and other armies hired Thracians as soldiers.
src: The Odrysian Kingdom, founded by Teres I in the early 5th century BCE, was a union of more than 40 Thracian tribes and 22 kingdoms
They were known as skilled horsemen / their soldiers were valued as mercenaries, particularly by the Macedonians and Romans

text: Nearly 2,000 years ago, their land became part of the Roman Empire, and some Roman emperors had Thracian families.
Over time the Thracians mixed with other peoples and became ancestors of people in south-eastern Europe.
src: 46 CE: Thracia becomes a Roman province / Several Roman and Byzantine emperors were wholly or partly of Thracian descent, among them Maximinus Thrax
Most likely the Thracians were assimilated into Roman and Byzantine society and became one of the ancestral groups of modern south-eastern Europeans

text: Thracian nobles were buried with their horses and chariots, to use again after death.
Today their tombs and their gold and silver treasures are found and studied in Bulgaria and Romania.
src: Noblemen were buried with their horses and chariots so that these could serve them again in the afterlife
Their tombs and gold and silver treasures, studied mainly in Bulgaria and Romania
